## What a Double Story (G+1) Porta Cabin Is, and When It Pays

A double story (G+1) porta cabin is a stacked modular building. The factory builds two cabin modules, and an engineered chassis, stacking columns and inter-module connections turn them into one two-floor structure on site. You get a ground floor, an upper floor and an external steel staircase, all on the plot area of a single cabin.

The buyer problem it solves is simple. Most working sites run out of ground before they run out of people. Vehicle lanes, material yards, cranes and stores claim the plot first. Meanwhile the team still needs offices, meeting rooms, records rooms and rest rooms. The G+1 build takes the one resource the site still has: the air above an existing cabin footprint.

So the page ahead answers the four questions G+1 buyers actually ask. First, when stacking beats buying two separate cabins. Second, what changes structurally, because a stacked cabin is not two standard cabins placed on top of each other. Third, what each of the six sizes really decides. Fourth, what the published price covers and what the structural quotation adds.

![Dark grey double storey porta cabin with external staircase](double-story-porta-cabin-dark-grey-exterior-hero.webp)

## The Ground Area Maths: One Footprint, Twice the Rooms

Work the numbers before you choose. A 20x10 ft cabin gives 200 sq ft of rooms on 200 sq ft of ground. Two of them give 400 sq ft of rooms but consume roughly 500 sq ft of plot once you add the gap and walkway between units. The G+1 version gives the same 400 sq ft of rooms on the original 200 sq ft plinth.

The table below puts the two routes side by side, because this single comparison decides most G+1 purchases.

| Decision factor | Two single storey cabins | One G+1 porta cabin |
|---|---|---|
| Ground area used | Roughly 2.5x one cabin footprint | One cabin footprint |
| Plinth and base work | Two plinths, two levelling jobs | One plinth, one levelling job |
| Team separation | Two doors across the yard | Two floors, one staircase apart |
| Structural scope | Standard single storey practice | Project structural calculation |
| Access | Ground level only | External stair, guards and landing |

Read the last two rows carefully. The stacked route saves ground but adds engineering scope and stair access. That trade is worth it on tight plots. It is unnecessary on open ones, which is why we say so plainly in the orientation section above.

## What Changes Structurally From a Single Storey Cabin

Here is the honest engineering core of this product. A single storey cabin never carries another building on its roof. A G+1 ground module does, so SAMAN re-engineers the load path from top to bottom rather than reusing single storey members.

The ground floor chassis becomes a two-storey transfer chassis. Its reference starting section is a 150x75x5 mm MS C-channel, which is substantially heavier than a standard cabin base. Transfer members and base stiffeners line up under the stacking posts of the upper module. Corner columns become stacking columns, with a 60x60x3 mm SHS reference section in place of standard single storey posts, and each module carries a reinforced ring beam that moves vertical and lateral loads into the stacking connections.

The upper floor deserves its own paragraph, because it is the most misunderstood part of a stacked cabin. It is not a roof with flooring laid over it. It is an engineered structural floor, checked for live load, deflection and vibration, with a 24 mm cement board or heavy deck walking surface. Only the top module carries the weather roof, with a positive slope and sealed penetrations. The lower module top is treated as inter-storey construction instead.

One rule ties all of this together. Every section named above is a reference starting section, and the final member sizes, foundation reactions, wind and seismic stability, connection plates and anchors come from project structural calculations. SAMAN publishes the reference sections so you can compare vendors honestly, and releases fabrication only against the approved structural package. Treat any G+1 quotation without that calculation step as incomplete.

![Side walkway and staircase view of a double storey porta cabin](double-story-porta-cabin-side-walkway-staircase.webp)

## Stairs, Access and Egress Are Engineered Scope

The staircase is part of the structure, not an accessory. Stair clear width, riser geometry, handrails, guards, landings and escape routes are set by the approved egress plan for your occupancy, and the stair, landing and guard steel is designed with the building. Doors on occupied floors open outward as the egress plan requires, and upper floor access is coordinated with the stair and landing system.

Openings follow the same discipline. Windows and service openings cannot cut stacking posts, transfer members or required bracing, so large openings get reinforcement shown on the approved shop drawings. If a layout sketch shows a window where a stacking column stands, the drawing changes before fabrication, never on site.

## Services Floor by Floor

Each floor runs its own services. Electrical wiring follows the protected copper schedule of 1.5, 2.5 and 4 sq.mm circuits with a distribution board, MCB and RCCB protection and earthing, engineered per floor to the approved load schedule. Ventilation and air-conditioning run floor by floor as well, with sealed service risers and no uncontrolled openings between storeys.

Plumbing stays excluded unless you order it. When you do, wet areas stack vertically where practical, so risers, vents and drainage stay short and serviceable, and every floor penetration receives waterproofing treatment as required. Decide toilets and pantries at drawing stage; they are simple to align between floors on paper and expensive to relocate after fabrication.

## What Buyers Put on Each Floor

The most common configuration is office over office: supervision and visitor handling below, engineering, documentation or management above. Plants and campuses also run office over store, keeping ground level for material receipt while records and quality teams sit upstairs. Marketing and administration setups use the upper floor for meetings, since visitors experience the stair once and the ground floor keeps daily traffic.

Know the boundary of this product as well. A single G+1 cabin serves one team or two, up to the 1,200 sq ft flagship. Project-scale worker housing with rows of rooms, kitchens and ablution blocks is a different product family, and our [labour colony](https://www.samanportable.com/product/labor-colony) pages cover those G+1 and G+2 accommodation blocks with their own capacity planning. Residential living layouts belong to the porta cabin house instead. Keeping those boundaries clear protects your specification and your budget.

## Scope: What Is Standard, Optional, Custom and Excluded

STANDARD scope covers the engineered stacked structure: transfer chassis, stacking columns, both floor structures, the top-storey weather roof, insulated envelope, interior lining, doors and windows per the approved opening schedule, the external stair package and the per-floor electrical baseline.

OPTIONAL scope covers partitions, furniture, air-conditioning units, stacked wet areas with the vertical plumbing riser, grills and mesh, and extra doors or windows where the structure allows them.

CUSTOM scope covers layouts, colours, cladding selection and opening positions, always through the approved drawing. EXCLUDED scope covers foundations, transport, unloading, site power supply and project-specific engineering and tests, which are quoted separately once your site details are known. Every option lands as a line item on the quotation, so you can add or remove scope and watch the effect.

## Transport, Unloading and Site Readiness

A G+1 cabin travels as separate modules and becomes a two-storey building during installation. Modules up to 20 ft ride a 20 ft open trailer, and 30 to 40 ft modules ride a 40 ft open trailer, with freight following the distance ladder in the Shipping tab. The 12 ft wide modules of the 40x12 ft size can classify as an over-dimensional consignment, and ODC charges stay estate-dependent until the route is confirmed.

Prepare the site before the trailers arrive. You need a level base built to the approved foundation drawing, clear approach and turning room for the trailer, working space for the crane during stacking, and a power point for the distribution board hook-up. Anchoring follows the structural package. The staircase side needs its clear strip, so mark it on the plinth plan from day one.

## How to Compare G+1 Quotations Line by Line

Cheap stacked-cabin quotes hide their savings in the structure, and you cannot see the structure in a photograph. So compare quotations on five numbers before you compare prices. Ask every vendor for the transfer chassis section under the ground module, and compare it against our published 150x75x5 mm reference. Ask for the stacking column section, against our 60x60x3 mm SHS reference. Ask what the upper floor is designed for, because a converted roof and an engineered floor look identical in a render and behave differently under a loaded file rack.

Then ask two scope questions. Does the quotation include project structural calculations, foundation reactions and an approved drawing set, or does it reuse single storey members without a check? And is the stair package, with guards, landings and egress geometry, inside the price or left as a site extra? A vendor who cannot answer these five points in writing is not quoting the same product. Ours are printed here, in the Specifications tab and in the versioned PDF, so you can hold the delivered building to the promise.

## Double Story Porta Cabin FAQs

### How is the price of a G+1 porta cabin calculated?

The planning ladder prices total built-up area across both floors at the published rate input of Rs 1,310 per sq ft with area band adjustments. A 20x10 ft G+1 therefore prices 400 sq ft, not 200. The final price follows the structural quotation for your site.

### Do I need a foundation for a double storey porta cabin?

Yes, and it is designed, not assumed. The G+1 structure concentrates both storeys into the ground module supports, so the base and anchoring follow the foundation drawing produced from project structural calculations. Simple levelled ground that serves a single cabin is not automatically enough.

### Can I put a G+1 porta cabin on a rooftop?

Only after your structural engineer confirms the slab can carry the stacked loads at the planned position, and only with crane access to that level. Share the building details with your enquiry and we will advise on feasibility before quoting.

### How long does delivery take?

Standard delivery takes 7 to 21 working days after order confirmation, plus transit per the Shipping tab. The structural approval step for your configuration is scheduled within the quotation, so the committed programme is stated there.

### Can the two floors have different uses?

Yes. Office over office is the most common split, followed by office over store. Each floor runs its own electrical circuits and ventilation, and stacked wet areas are available as optional scope where drawings allow.

### Are custom sizes possible beyond the six published options?

Yes. The six-size ladder covers standard footprints from 20x10 ft to 30x20 ft. Other footprints follow the same engineering route against an approved drawing and quotation.
